_comment: Tolerances for the equivalence run (tests/acceptance/run_recipe.py). There are no measured
numbers in this file on purpose: the thing this package is checked against is a the research code
run of the IDENTICAL configuration, re-measured on the same instrument beside it, and its
values are written OUT to reference.json by the harness rather than written down here.
domain_ppl.tol_rel   = 0.02. Relative gap allowed between the two runs'
direct_perplexity.overall.mean_perplexity on the held-out
chat-formatted Q&A set (never comparable with held-out raw-prose
perplexity, a different quantity).
seed_drift.tol_abs_pct = 1.0. Absolute gap allowed, in percentage POINTS, between the two
runs' WikiText-2 drift over the full test split (window 2048, stride
512 -- the companion's wikitext2_perplexity(n_windows=0)), each read
against the base model's perplexity measured in the same run.
content_curve.epochs / tol_rel = the first 5 epochs, each within 0.5 % of the reference's
per-epoch content loss. That is the window in which two bf16 runs of
the same objective still agree to three decimals; later epochs drift
chaotically for reasons that are not a defect, which is why the
endpoint is checked through perplexity instead.
What the tolerances cover, none of which is a defect: bf16 non-determinism between two
implementations of the same objective; the research code's mu fast path, which is mathematically
exact but not bit-reproducing; and ordinary run-to-run variation on one card. They are not
to be widened to accommodate a run -- a number outside them is a finding.
